nodes.title: Inner product of bit strings modulo two

nodes.summary: For every set $Q \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^n$ of fewer than $n$ points there is $u \neq 0$ with $u\cdot x = 0$ for all $x \in Q$ (the linear map $u \mapsto (u\cdot x)_{x\in Q}$ has a nontrivial kernel). Hence $x \mapsto s\cdot x$ and $x \mapsto (s+u)\cdot x$ agree on $Q$, and evaluations at the points of $Q$ cannot tell $s$ from $s + u$.
nodes.title: Classical evaluations: fewer than `n` never determine `s`

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{Z}_2^n \to \mathbb{Z}_2$, the amplitude of $|t\rangle$ in $H_n O_f H_n |0\cdots0\rangle$, where $O_f |x\rangle = (-1)^{f(x)} |x\rangle$, is This is equation (3.6) of Cleve, Ekert, Macchiavello and Mosca with the normalisation restored, and the special case of Fourier sampling with respect to $g = (-1)^f$ in Bernstein and Vazirani (Theorem 8.4.2: outcome $s$ with probability $|\hat f(s)|^2$ for…
nodes.title: Amplitudes of Fourier sampling

nodes.summary: If $f(x) = s\cdot x + b$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Z}_2^n$, then one query of Fourier sampling produces exactly the state $(-1)^b |s\rangle$, so measuring it returns the hidden string $s$ with certainty.
nodes.title: Bernstein–Vazirani algorithm

nodes.summary: If $f : \mathbb{Z}_2^n \to \mathbb{Z}_2$ is balanced (it takes the values $0$ and $1$ equally often), the amplitude of $|0\cdots0\rangle$ in $H_n O_f H_n |0\cdots0\rangle$ is $0$, so measuring never gives $0\cdots0$. If $f$ is constant, the outcome is $0\cdots0$ with probability $1$ (constant case). One query therefore decides with certainty whether a function promised to be constant or balanced is constant.
nodes.title: Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm, balanced case

nodes.summary: `(-1)^(s·x)` is a Hadamard matrix of order `2ⁿ` in the sense of Mathlib's `Matrix.IsHadamard`: its entries are `±1` and its rows are orthogonal, by orthogonality of the parity characters (Bernstein and Vazirani, Section 8.4).
nodes.title: The sign matrix is a Hadamard matrix

nodes.summary: If $f(x) = s\cdot x + b$ for all $x$, then measuring $H_n O_f H_n |0\cdots0\rangle$ in the computational basis gives the outcome $t$ with probability $1$ if $t = s$ and $0$ otherwise (Born rule: the squared modulus of the amplitude).
nodes.title: The Bernstein–Vazirani algorithm outputs `s` with certainty

nodes.summary: If $f$ is constant, measuring $H_n O_f H_n |0\cdots0\rangle$ gives $0\cdots0$ with probability $1$ (Cleve, Ekert, Macchiavello and Mosca, Section 3, after equation (3.6)): a constant function is the case $s = 0$ of the Bernstein–Vazirani problem.
nodes.title: Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm, constant case

nodes.summary: The reversible oracle $|x\rangle|b\rangle \mapsto |x\rangle|b + f(x)\rangle$, applied to a state whose amplitude at $(x, b)$ is $a(x)(-1)^b$ (target qubit in $|0\rangle - |1\rangle$), multiplies the amplitude at $(x, b)$ by $(-1)^{f(x)}$. So one call to the reversible oracle acts as the phase oracle on the first register (Cleve, Ekert, Macchiavello and Mosca, equations (3.3)–(3.5)). The Lean statement records this…
nodes.title: Phase kickback
